name: image-cropper
pattern: A headless image cropper that operates rectangle movement, resizing, and image zoom with native buttons and native ranges. Do not use a two-dimensional slider role or application role
responsibility: Manages the selection rectangle, image zoom, and image position and provides CSS custom properties, native-control values, a crop range in the source image, and a cancelable commit event. Does not fetch, generate, or render images, generate elements, or specify layout

authorMarkup.root: An HTMLElement with data-controller="image-cropper" and role="group". Name its purpose with aria-label or aria-labelledby. Do not use a button or input itself as root

targets.viewport: Exactly one HTMLElement that is the basis for selection operations, parent of image, selection, and resize, with an authored id
targets.image: Exactly one native img inside viewport. The user supplies src, optional srcset / sizes, non-empty alt, and draggable="false". Do not make it a child of selection / resize
targets.selection: Exactly one native button[type=button] inside viewport, an operable element overlapping the selection rectangle for movement. Give it a name explaining that activation focuses position controls and reference xControl and yControl ids with aria-controls
targets.resize: Exactly one native button[type=button] inside viewport at the rectangle block-end / inline-end corner. Make it a sibling of selection, give it a name explaining that activation focuses size controls, and write aria-controls referencing widthControl / heightControl
targets.xControl: Exactly one named input[type=range] for adjusting distance from inline-start, with an id and aria-controls referencing viewport
targets.yControl: Exactly one named input[type=range] for adjusting distance from the top edge, with an id and aria-controls referencing viewport
targets.widthControl: Exactly one named input[type=range] for adjusting selection width, with an id and aria-controls referencing viewport
targets.heightControl: Exactly one named input[type=range] for adjusting selection height, with an id and aria-controls referencing viewport
targets.zoomControl: Exactly one named input[type=range] for adjusting image zoom, with an id and aria-controls referencing viewport
targets.instructions: Exactly one non-empty HTMLElement whose user-authored text explains selection / resize arrows, Shift+arrows, +/-, Escape, and Enter / Space. Do not generate operation instructions

authorMarkup.controls: The five ranges are required non-drag pointer / keyboard paths for all features. Number / text inputs are not required. Make the full range track clickable/tappable and do not disable pointer-events outside the thumb. Controls may be grouped in native details inside root. Use a structure where summary opens to reach every control and button activation opens ancestors in behavior.activation order before focusing. Do not nest mutually exclusive details such that a focus target's ancestors cannot be opened together. Do not put ranges inside viewport. All five ranges must share one form owner or all have null form owners
authorMarkup.labels: Name each range with label, aria-label, or aria-labelledby. Convey in the label or user description that position/dimension units are percentages of viewport and zoom is a multiplier. Name buttons with text, aria-label, or aria-labelledby. The controller does not infer labels, descriptions, or image content
authorMarkup.cssGeometry: Write user CSS so zoom=1 and offsetX=offsetY=0 make the full source image coincide with viewport. Match viewport and image aspect ratios, omit border / padding, and do not crop the image with object-fit:cover. Rotation, skew, and flip transforms on viewport or ancestors are outside the scope. Use horizontal writing-mode for viewport and support LTR / RTL. Do not mirror the image itself in RTL. Position selection / resize from computed results. The user CSS owns decoration, dimensions, position, overflow, and touch-action
authorMarkup.resources: The user and browser own image loading, failure messaging, and candidate selection. The controller does not use naturalWidth, naturalHeight, image URL, or pixel data as state. Preserve normalized values when the image changes. The user assigns value to return to a new image's initial range

semanticElements: Every target exists exactly once as a distinct element belonging to the same root, with viewport / image / selection / resize containment following authorMarkup.targets
image is an img with non-empty alt and no tabindex / contenteditable, selection / resize are native buttons, and the five controls are native input[type=range]
root, buttons, and ranges have names from authorMarkup.labels, and instructions is non-empty. Every aria-labelledby id resolves in the same ownerDocument to non-empty text

Authored roles agree with group on root, button on buttons, and slider on ranges; controls are not permanently excluded with aria-hidden=true / hidden. Native buttons / ranges do not require authored role
Authored button type is button and image draggable is false. Missing values are handled by completion
step and zoomStep are positive finite numbers; minWidth / minHeight are finite numbers greater than 0 and at most 100; maxZoom is at least 1 and 100 * maxZoom is finite

value is an object with seven finite numbers: x, y, width, height, zoom, offsetX, and offsetY. Ignore unknown keys; missing or non-numeric required keys are invalid. Stimulus Object value attributes contain valid JSON
The five ranges have the same form owner. Do not mix targets from a nested separate image-cropper on one image
contractValidation.timing: Validate on connect, target addition/removal, Stimulus value changes, and immediately before operations / public setters. Do not warn about CSS load order or a temporarily zero-sized viewport as markup violations
contractValidation.invalidMarkup: For initially invalid markup, do not set output, completion, or operation listeners and issue one enhancement-disabled warning while connected. When valid markup becomes invalid, restore an in-progress preview to the last committed value, release capture, remove operation listeners, and disable enhancement. Keep already synchronized attributes and values. Revalidate after target/value repair or reconnection. Do not throw. Do not replace Stimulus's handling of its own JSON syntax errors

completion.warning: Supplement only missing static attributes and list them in the standard English wording. Issue one completion warning while connected using a separate flag from the enhancement-disabled warning. Do not warn for complete markup. Do not overwrite authored ids, names, or relationship attributes

contractValidation.completionExempt: Assign operation ids without collisions. Compose the instructions id into selection / resize aria-describedby while preserving existing tokens. Do not warn for range value, min, max, or step=any because they synchronize state/settings. details.open=true used to reveal a focus target on button activation is behavioral and does not warn. Do not duplicate native range values in ARIA value attributes. Read disabled from native attributes rather than outputting synchronized state

value.description: ImageCropperValue. Rectangle and image position use viewport axes where 100 is the full axis; zoom is a multiplier. The HTML attribute is an initial value and external assignment path; do not write operation results back to it

step.description: Change for one selection / resize arrow operation (viewport %). Delegate native range key increments to the browser

zoomStep.description: Zoom difference for one + / - operation on selection / resize

maxZoom.description: Maximum image zoom. The minimum is fixed at 1

types.ImageCropperValue: { x: number; y: number; width: number; height: number; zoom: number; offsetX: number; offsetY: number }. x / offsetX use inline-start; y / offsetY use the top edge
types.ImageCropperSourceRect: { x: number; y: number; width: number; height: number }. The full source image is width 1 and height 1; x / y always use the physical top-left. Do not round pixels to integers
types.ImageCropperChangeDetail: { value: ImageCropperValue; previousValue: ImageCropperValue; sourceRect: ImageCropperSourceRect; previousSourceRect: ImageCropperSourceRect; reason: 'pointer' | 'keyboard' }. Export all three types from src/index.ts

value.description: Null until the first valid connection. Thereafter return a copy of the current value, including the preview during an operation. The setter normalizes and commits all seven values together without dispatching an event or moving focus. It is a no-op while disconnected or when markup / settings are invalid. An invalid object preserves the last committed value and interrupts an in-progress preview

sourceRect.description: A copy of the source-image range calculated from the current value and direction. Null until the first valid connection. Includes the preview

zoom.description: Current zoom. Null until the first valid connection. The setter interrupts pending operations, applies behavior.zoom from the last committed value, leaves the rectangle unchanged, and synchronizes only zoom and offsets. It is a no-op while disconnected or when markup / settings are invalid. Non-finite numbers preserve the last committed value. Do not dispatch an event or move focus

image-cropper:beforechange.when: Immediately before committing a trusted operation. If a preview exists, first restore the pre-operation committed value before notifying
image-cropper:beforechange.effect: When preventDefault() is called, do not apply the candidate; keep value, sourceRect, all ranges, and custom properties at pre-operation values and do not dispatch change

image-cropper:change.when: After beforechange allows the candidate and it is synchronized to every output

events.preview: Pointermove over the image and continuous native-range input update only the preview. Commit once on image pointerup or native-range change. Dispatch neither event for equal operations at range boundaries
events.programmatic: Public setters, Stimulus value changes, initialization, settings changes, form reset, reconnection, and preview interruption do not dispatch custom events
events.reason: Operations beginning with image drag or range pointerdown use pointer. Operations beginning with keydown use keyboard. Trusted native adjustments without pointerdown / keydown (such as AT) are classified as keyboard. This API does not infer hardware type
events.synthetic: Operation events with isTrusted=false do not commit state. When synthetic input / change changes only a native value, restore it to the controller's current value without dispatching a custom event
events.snapshot: Input objects, getters, beforechange detail, and change detail do not share objects with internal state. Mutating beforechange detail cannot change the candidate. A public setter / disconnect / target change inside a beforechange listener takes precedence over the candidate; do not overwrite with the old candidate or dispatch change

behavior.stateOwner: Use the controller's committed value as the state source. An in-progress operation has an independent start snapshot and preview. Native ranges and CSS are projections of that state. Derive sourceRect rather than storing it
behavior.configuration: On the first valid connection, normalize the latest value attribute or default using current settings. A value-attribute change is a new batch input; a settings-only change re-normalizes the last committed value. Handle simultaneous attribute changes using the latest settings and value together. For invalid settings / value attributes, preserve the last committed value and disable enhancement. On repair, use new value-attribute input when present; otherwise resume from the preserved committed value. Do not update the initial snapshot on form reset
behavior.direction: Use viewport computed direction. x / offsetX use its inline-start; preserve all seven values when direction changes and derive sourceRect from the new direction. Direction changes alone dispatch no custom event or focus movement. Delegate native range behavior to each element's browser default
behavior.normalization: For batch assignment, clamp width / height from each minimum to 100, then x to 0..100-width, y to 0..100-height, zoom to 1..maxZoom, and offsetX / offsetY to 100-100*zoom..0. Correct finite out-of-range numbers and do not commit non-finite inputs or results. Do not round pointer fractions
behavior.singleField: A single-control change does not move other rectangle values. Clamp x to 0..100-width, y to 0..100-height, width to minWidth..100-x, and height to minHeight..100-y. Do not move position automatically to increase size
behavior.zoom: A zoom-only operation preserves selection x/y/width/height. With center p=(x+width/2,y+height/2), current zoom z, and new zoom z', calculate offsetX'=p.x-((p.x-offsetX)/z)*z' and offsetY' likewise. Clamp each to 100-100*z'..0. Preserve the image point at the center as far as possible while covering the whole viewport. When edge correction is needed, prioritize coverage over center preservation. Both offsets are 0 at zoom=1
behavior.sourceCoordinates: LTR: sourceRect.x=(x-offsetX)/(100*zoom). RTL: sourceRect.x=1-(x+width-offsetX)/(100*zoom). In both directions y=(y-offsetY)/(100*zoom), width=width/(100*zoom), and height=height/(100*zoom). Keep each edge within source-image 0..1 without floating-point escape. Do not mirror the image itself
behavior.directPointer: Accept only the primary pointer's left button on selection / resize. Save start position, current seven values, viewport rectangle, direction, and disabled state, and capture the pointer on the start element. No-op when capture cannot be obtained. Change selection x/y from the start delta and resize width/height from the delta. Convert viewport rendered width/height deltas to percentages and reverse horizontal delta sign in RTL. Keep resize inline-start / top fixed. Do not jump to the grabbed point. Do not mix another pointer into an existing operation
behavior.directCompletion: Apply through the final pointerup coordinates, release capture, and commit once when start and final candidates differ. Discard preview and restore start values on pointercancel, unexpected lostpointercapture, Escape, window blur, or geometry / direction / disabled changes. Ordinary lostpointercapture after pointerup does not cancel commitment. Allow subsequent click activation only when the pointer did not move from its start. If pointer coordinates moved even once, do not move focus on that operation's subsequent click, including when the value stayed at a boundary or returned to its original position. Suppress exactly one click in that pointer sequence and do not carry it to the next trusted pointerdown / button keydown. Direct pointer operations do not prevent native focus and the controller does not focus itself
behavior.range: Synchronize the five range value / min / max and step=any properties with controller state. Do not replace native range keyboard, pointer, or AT value changes. Take a start snapshot from the primary pointer's left button or a keydown listed in nativeControls, preview the corresponding value on trusted input, and commit on trusted change. Do not retake the snapshot for key repeats within one range operation. If pointerup / keyup arrives before native change, do not commit; when equal, return to idle while retaining only the origin classification. This prevents adjusting from lingering on a boundary operation without change. A trusted input / change without an origin commits immediately as one native adjustment; do not notify again for an equal later change. Treat Escape, pointercancel, and blur / window blur before completion as interruption. A blur after native change has completed is a no-op. Discard a completed origin on the next operation, blur, or invalidation
behavior.rangeBounds: xControl is 0..100-width, yControl is 0..100-height, widthControl is minWidth..100-x, heightControl is minHeight..100-y, and zoomControl is 1..maxZoom. Keep the value when min equals max. Set range attributes before synchronizing value and do not treat temporary native sanitization as a separate state change. Do not add aria-valuenow / min / max / valuetext
behavior.activation: On a trusted click without drag (including native click from Enter / Space), focus enabled xControl for selection or yControl if unavailable; focus enabled widthControl for resize or heightControl if unavailable. No-op when no corresponding enabled control exists. Walk ancestors from the focus target to root, open closed native details with open=true from outermost inward, then focus during the same activation. Do not add open/close-only targets, ARIA, or custom events and do not prevent native toggle. Keep details opened by activation open; do not close them on disconnect / reset. This operation does not change crop values and interrupts any pending preview first
behavior.disabled: Read native disabled state from disabled attributes and fieldset through :disabled. Ignore disabled origins. When xControl / yControl / widthControl / heightControl / zoomControl is disabled, image operations do not change that field. A disabled selection / resize stops only that operation element. Do not stop operations from enabled ranges or the public API. Interrupt the entire operation if disabled during operation. The controller does not overwrite disabled
behavior.interruptions: Interrupt a pending preview before accepting another operation. Ignore another pointer during direct drag rather than treating it as a new operation. Public setters, settings / target changes, and uncanceled form reset invalidate old operations. Exclude old capture / deferred callbacks by revision. While a stale range's physical operation continues and on its ending change, restore the native value to the current committed value and consume it without a custom event. After physical-operation cleanup, a new native adjustment without an origin follows normal range rules. New trusted pointerdown / keydown does not inherit stale records. After beforechange, directly revalidate target identity/containment, settings, connection, direction, and disabled state; discard candidate application and change if any changed. Do not use MutationObserver delivery alone for reentrancy detection
behavior.interruptionTiming: Re-read disabled and direction involved in an operation before each operation event and after dispatching beforechange. For direct pointer operations, also compare viewport left / top / width / height with the start snapshot. Interrupt on difference for that event and do not apply an old delta to new geometry. Continuous geometry polling and image-load subscription are unnecessary. Invalidate on target / value changes from Stimulus callbacks too
behavior.formReset: Keep the initial snapshot committed on the first valid connection. For associated-form reset, check defaultPrevented after delivery; when canceled, change nothing including preview. When not canceled, normalize the initial snapshot with current settings after native reset and commit it. Do not dispatch an event or move focus. If a public setter / settings change / target replacement / disconnect occurs before post-reset synchronization, it takes precedence and delayed work must not restore the initial value
behavior.geometryUnavailable: Do not start direct pointer operations when viewport width or height is 0, non-finite, or the document window cannot be obtained. Interrupt an active operation. Normalized values and range / keyboard / public API operations do not depend on viewport pixel dimensions
behavior.exclusions: Do not select, fetch, decode, or upload image files; create canvas, Blob, or Data URLs; rotate / flip the source image; provide fixed crop-frame mode, aspect-ratio lock, independent image pan, or wheel / pinch interpretation. Do not suppress browser default wheel / pinch behavior

keyboard.selection: On focused selection, unmodified ArrowLeft / ArrowRight move horizontally and ArrowUp / ArrowDown move vertically by step. In LTR, Right increases x and Left decreases it; Down increases y and Up decreases it. Reverse horizontal numeric changes in RTL. Shift with the same arrows changes width/height by the same sign while fixing inline-start / top
keyboard.resize: On focused resize, unmodified ArrowLeft / ArrowRight change width and ArrowUp / ArrowDown change height by step. In LTR, Right and Down increase while Left and Up decrease. Reverse width changes in RTL. Ignore Shift combinations
keyboard.zoom: On selection / resize, + or = adds zoomStep and - subtracts it. Allow only Shift needed to type +. No-op when zoomControl is disabled
keyboard.nativeControls: Delegate range ArrowLeft / ArrowRight / ArrowUp / ArrowDown / Home / End / PageUp / PageDown to the browser. Do not double-correct step=any increments or engine differences in RTL. Native button Enter / Space performs activation
keyboard.navigationAndCancel: Preserve DOM-order native focus movement for Tab / Shift+Tab; do not add a trap or roving model. Escape discards only its own in-progress preview. Receive Escape during direct drag from the ownerDocument window without depending on button focus. Call preventDefault only for handled direct-operation arrow/zoom keys and Escape and do not stop propagation. Do not process a key for a disabled axis. Suppress scrolling when an enabled axis reaches an equal boundary and do not dispatch a custom event
keyboard.excluded: For IME (isComposing or keyCode=229), Alt / Control / Meta modifiers, and other keys, do not perform controller-specific direct operations or preventDefault. Do not interfere with native control operation; its trusted input / change follows behavior.range

managedMarkup.static: Supplement only attributes in contractValidation.completion / completionExempt. Preserve authored names, descriptions, alt, ids, and aria-controls
managedMarkup.native: Synchronize the five range min / max / step / value properties. Do not rewrite value content attribute, name, form, disabled, or tabindex. Set details open only for behavior.activation. Do not add unknown two-dimensional ARIA roles or value attributes to root / buttons / ranges
managedMarkup.customProperties: Output --image-cropper-x, --image-cropper-y, --image-cropper-width, --image-cropper-height, --image-cropper-zoom, --image-cropper-offset-x, and --image-cropper-offset-y as unitless finite numbers on root. The user determines CSS placement, conversion to dimension units, and image rendering
managedMarkup.content: Do not generate innerHTML / textContent / output content. Write only the seven custom properties to style. Do not write position, width, height, transform, overflow, touch-action, or class

stateOutputs.root: data-state=idle when there is no preview, moving during selection pointer operation, resizing during resize pointer operation, and adjusting during a pending range operation. This is the component's single operation state
stateOutputs.ownership: Only root data-state and the seven managedMarkup.customProperties values are controller-owned CSS output. Do not add per-target data-state, data-disabled, or image loading state

lifecycle: Reset warningIssued / completionWarningIssued on each connection and register listeners after validation. Do not start operations when TargetConnected / TargetDisconnected runs before connect
Track target additions and removals with Stimulus callbacks and coalesce multiple changes in reconcile. Clean up old-element listeners / capture before adopting new elements

Subscribe to pointer, keydown / keyup, click, input / change, blur, and form reset only while connected. Global listeners use ownerDocument / its window and do not capture operations from another root

Even when root remains in the DOM, disconnect disables all listeners and deferred work, releases capture, and restores the last committed value. Set root data-state to idle. Retain generated ids / ARIA / custom properties / range values

On reconnection of the same instance, do not repeat initialization and preserve the last committed value. If the value attribute changes while disconnected, use its latest value on reconnection. Do not duplicate listeners or custom events
Check connection and operation revisions for each capture / deferred callback / beforechange so stale work cannot commit another operation. Do not move focus with a timer

consumerIntegration.imageGeneration: Multiply sourceRect x / width by source-image width and y / height by source-image height to produce the source rectangle for image generation. For an 800x600 image, sourceRect={x:0.375,y:0.375,width:0.25,height:0.25} yields source x=300,y=225,width=200,height=150. The user JS obtains natural size, checks loading success, rounds integers, chooses output size, and handles canvas and CORS
consumerIntegration.css: Use each % output for selection inline-start / top / width / height. Start the image from offset percentages and make its width/height zoom times viewport. On zoom changes, keep the selection's visual position/dimensions and enlarge the image beneath it
consumerIntegration.externalControls: Additional number inputs or custom UI are optional. User JS can read/write value / zoom. Because the programmatic API dispatches no event, the caller handles custom UI notifications. Required native ranges cannot simply be removed
consumerIntegration.nested: Events bubble. When receiving them outside a nested same-type controller, limit the root with :self or event.target === event.currentTarget

observations.environment: macOS Safari + VoiceOver, Windows Firefox + NVDA, iOS Safari + VoiceOver, and Android Chrome
observations.item: Native range names/values, navigation between controls, touch scrolling, and track-tap ergonomics
observations.impact: Five named native ranges, geometry, keyboard behavior, and pointercancel restoration are fixed. Inoperable controls or missing values are defects, not successful observations; headless tests do not verify real-device speech.

acceptanceCriteria: Require WCAG 2.2 AA and verify that controller-owned name/role/value synchronization, keyboard paths for all operations, pointer cancellation, non-drag pointer paths, and focus visibility are not obstructed. The user owns image alternative content, descriptions, contrast, target size, focus indicators, and placement according to authorMarkup
AAA 2.1.3 Keyboard (No Exception): movement, resizing, and zoom each have a named native range and a direct keyboard equivalent. No pointer-only feature exists
AAA 3.2.5 Change on Request: only explicit selection / resize button activation moves focus. Connection, synchronization, reconnection, reset, and timers do not move focus

WCAG 2.5.7: clicking/tapping the five range tracks alone changes position, width, height, and zoom. Numeric inputs are optional, but no non-drag control may be omitted. The catalog and three-engine tests verify this independently of direct drag
WCAG 2.5.2: direct drag commits on pointerup and restores start values on Escape / pointercancel. Native ranges commit on native change. Do not dispatch change from a canceled preview

Verify normalization, image coverage, center-based zoom, and LTR / RTL conversion to physical top-left source coordinates with fixed expected values. Keep source rectangles inside the image and do not write CSS output directly to user layout properties

Verify beforechange → value/range/CSS synchronization → change order, cancellation, equal values, synthetic events, public API, disabled state, reentrant setters, target replacement, disconnect / reconnect, and form reset

Run component tests and catalog scenarios in Chromium, Firefox, and WebKit. Check direct pointer capture and native-range event order in all three engines; do not replace failures with unverified observations

observation / image-cropper-native-at: observe native range name/value announcements in the catalog, guidance when moving from buttons to ranges, and distinguishing five controls using macOS Safari + VoiceOver, Windows Firefox + NVDA, and iOS Safari + VoiceOver. Unverified. Native button/range roles, five required controls, native min/max/value, and equivalent paths for all features are fixed; do not revisit them based on announcement wording, duplication, or timing. Treat inoperable controls or missing values as implementation defects or needs_replan, not successful observation

observation / image-cropper-touch: observe touch-action and page-scrolling ergonomics from user CSS and range-track taps on real-device iOS Safari and Android Chrome. Unverified. Public geometry, keyboard, ARIA, required markup, and pointercancel restoration are independent of the result. Do not introduce gestures or suppress wheel / pinch based on this observation

testMatrix.description: Disable invalid target counts/types/containment, accessible names, instructions, settings/value, and missing native ranges
Initial values, seven custom properties, range bounds/value, authored-attribute preservation, and no CSS/content generation
Completion warning for static attributes, behavioral-attribute exemptions, no warning for complete markup, and reconnection
min/max, single-field and batch-setter clamping, zoom center, image coverage, source conversion, and fractions
Logical direction for direct key/pointer, physical RTL sourceRect coordinates, and native-range default behavior preservation
Movement, Shift resize, resize handle, +/-, IME/modifier exclusion, and Tab/Enter/Space/Escape. Open closed details before focusing an enabled range without changing values or custom events
Operate five ranges with trusted clicks without drag and verify each state and sourceRect change; reach the same features with native keyboard operation

Trusted selection/resize drag, grab offset, pointer capture, final position, preview, pointercancel/Escape/lost capture. A drag returning to its original pointer coordinates leaves values/events unchanged. Distinguish focus results for boundary no-change drag and ordinary click
Commit order, detail, cancellation, equal values, bubbling, and event suppression during preview

Native range input/change, pointer and keyboard origins, originless native adjustment, and synthetic-event value restoration. Return to idle on equal track click/boundary key and do not carry the prior preview into the next snapshot
Native/fieldset disabled, direct-operation suppression for affected axes, invalidation during operation, and public API independence
Invalidation from setter/settings/target/direction/geometry changes, changes inside beforechange, and delayed native events. Accept a new native adjustment after stale physical operation cleanup
Disconnect with DOM retained, capture/listener cleanup, reconnection, target replacement, reset cancellation/race, nested instances, and multiple instances
value / zoom / sourceRect, copy isolation, invalid setters, programmatic silence, and range preservation when replacing an image
